breakfast.name: Boerewors and Eggs
ingredients: Tomato, onion, chilli (for a chakalaka side)
Bread (white rolls -- vetkoek or a roll)
instructions: Boerewors means farmer sausage in Afrikaans: boer (farmer) + wors (sausage)
Boerewors is a coiled sausage made from beef (minimum 90% meat by law)
The spice blend is the identity: coriander seed, cloves, nutmeg, allspice
The coriander seed is the dominant and defining boerewors flavor
Grilled on the braai (barbecue): the correct cooking method
Pan-fried: the indoor compromise, still good
Served with fried eggs -- the boerewors and egg breakfast
Tomato and onion or chakalaka (spiced tomato-bean relish) as the side
Boerewors is a protected food product in South Africa -- strict quality standards
breakfast.description: South African spiced farmer sausage breakfast -- boerewors (coiled beef sausage seasoned with coriander seed, cloves, nutmeg, and allspice) grilled on the braai or pan-fried, served with fried eggs. Boerewors is a legally protected food product in South Africa: minimum 90% meat. The coriander seed is the defining flavor. Served with chakalaka (spiced tomato-bean relish) or just tomato and onion.

breakfast.name: Vetkoek with Mince
ingredients: Vetkoek dough: flour, yeast, salt, water, oil
Onion, tomato, curry powder (for the mince)
instructions: Vetkoek means fat cake in Afrikaans: vet (fat) + koek (cake)
A deep-fried dough ball that is the staple street food of South Africa
The dough is a simple yeast dough -- flour, yeast, salt, water
Fried in hot oil until golden and puffed -- the center stays soft
Split open while hot -- the steam escapes, creating a pocket
Filled with savory spiced mince (kerrievruchte -- curry mince)
The curry mince filling: onion, tomato, beef mince, curry powder
Sweet version: vetkoek with butter and golden syrup or apricot jam
Sold at South African rugby grounds, school tuck shops, and markets
Vetkoek is comfort food -- deeply loved across all South African communities
breakfast.description: South African deep-fried dough balls -- vetkoek (vet = fat, koek = cake in Afrikaans), a simple yeast dough fried until golden and puffed, split open and filled with spiced curry mince (onion, tomato, beef, curry powder). The sweet version uses butter and golden syrup or apricot jam. Ubiquitous street food: sold at rugby games, school tuck shops, and markets across all communities.

breakfast.name: Pap and Chakalaka
ingredients: Mealie pap (white maize porridge -- ground maize meal)
Chakalaka (spiced tomato, onion, bean, and carrot relish)
Salt, butter or milk (for the pap)
instructions: Pap is the South African maize porridge -- a legacy of Nguni and Sotho agriculture
Maize is not indigenous to Africa -- it arrived with Portuguese traders from the Americas
But maize became the fundamental starch of southern Africa over 400 years
Mealie pap: from mealie (South African English for maize) + pap (porridge)
Three textures: stywe (stiff, moldable), slap (soft, pouring consistency), and krummel (crumbly)
For breakfast: slap pap (soft porridge) with butter and milk -- the simplest
Chakalaka: a spiced relish of tomatoes, onions, beans, and carrots with chilli
Chakalaka is township-origin food -- a relish made from affordable ingredients
Pap + chakalaka: the combination that crosses all South African communities
Also eaten at the braai: stiff pap served as a side with meat
breakfast.description: South African maize porridge with spiced relish -- mealie pap (ground white maize cooked to slap/soft consistency for breakfast with butter and milk, or stiff/stywe for the braai) served with chakalaka (township-origin spiced relish of tomatoes, onions, beans, and carrots). Maize arrived via Portuguese traders but became the fundamental starch of southern Africa. Pap + chakalaka crosses all community boundaries.

imageCredit.author: philipp from cape town, south africa

breakfast.name: Rusks (Beskuit)
instructions: Rusks are the South African dried biscuit -- hard, dry, meant for dunking in coffee
The Afrikaans name: beskuit (biscuit)
Origin: the Great Trek and the Voortrekker tradition of dried food for long journeys
The Voortrekkers needed food that would not spoil -- rusks were ideal
Made as a loaf first, then sliced and dried in the oven overnight
The drying takes 8-12 hours at very low temperature -- the moisture is removed entirely
The result: a hard, dry biscuit that keeps for months
Dunked in coffee or tea until just soft -- the South African morning ritual
Buttermilk rusks: the most beloved variety (Anne's original buttermilk rusk)
All-bran rusks: with fiber and crunch -- the healthier version
breakfast.description: South African hard dried biscuits -- loaf baked first, then sliced and dried in the oven at low heat for 8-12 hours until all moisture is removed. Dunked in hot coffee or tea until just soft: the South African morning ritual. Voortrekker origin: long-life food for the Great Trek. Buttermilk rusks are the most beloved variety; all-bran rusks the healthier version.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Rainer Zenz assumed (based on copyright claims).

lunch.name: Braai (South African Barbecue)
ingredients: Chicken pieces (marinated with peri-peri or lemon)
instructions: The braai is not just cooking -- it is a South African cultural institution
Braai means to grill or barbecue in Afrikaans -- the word covers the event, not just the method
The braai is a social event: friends gather around the fire, drinks in hand
September 24: National Braai Day (Heritage Day) -- a public holiday
The fire: wood or charcoal -- gas braai is not traditional South African braai
The wood: rooikrans, sweetwood, or other hardwoods -- the wood type matters
The hierarchy: boerewors goes on first (quick and forgiving), then chicken, then chops
Sosaties: South African lamb and apricot kebabs -- Cape Malay origin
Braaibroodjie: the grilled cheese sandwich toasted over the braai coals
Everyone at a South African braai claims to know the correct way to manage the fire
lunch.description: The South African braai (barbecue) is a cultural institution, not just cooking -- a social event around a wood or charcoal fire. September 24 is National Braai Day (Heritage Day). Boerewors, lamb chops, marinated chicken, and sosaties (Cape Malay lamb-apricot kebabs) are the standard. Gas braai is not traditional. Braaibroodjie (grilled cheese sandwich over the coals) is the side. Everyone knows the correct fire management.

lunch.name: Bunny Chow
ingredients: Unsliced white bread (a quarter or half loaf)
Curry: lamb, bean, or chicken curry (Durban-style)
instructions: Bunny chow is the Durban curry in bread -- one of South Africa most iconic street foods
Origin: Durban Indian community, 1940s-1950s -- the exact origin is debated
One theory: Indian laborers brought curry to work in hollowed bread (no utensils needed)
Another theory: Durban restaurants used bread instead of plates during apartheid
Durban is the city with the largest Indian population outside India
The Indian labor history: brought from India (1860s) to work the KwaZulu-Natal sugar cane fields
Durban curry: distinct style -- bright turmeric, masala spice, distinctive Durban heat
Bean bunny: the vegetarian version -- butter beans in masala
Lamb bunny: the classic -- braised lamb in Durban curry sauce
The bread: a specific unsliced white loaf is hollowed; the scooped bread is the lid
The eating method: use the bread lid and the bread walls to scoop the curry
lunch.description: Durban curry in hollowed white bread -- a quarter or half loaf of unsliced white bread scooped out, filled with Durban-style curry (lamb, bean, or chicken with bright turmeric and masala heat), with the scooped bread as the lid. Origin: the Durban Indian community (1940s-1950s), shaped by the Indian labor history of KwaZulu-Natal. Durban has the largest Indian population outside India. Eat with the bread lid and walls.

lunch.name: Potjiekos (Pot Food)
ingredients: Lamb, chicken, or oxtail (tough cuts -- need long cooking)
Seasonal vegetables (potatoes, sweet potato, carrots, butternut)
Red wine (South African -- Pinotage or Shiraz)
instructions: Potjiekos means pot food in Afrikaans: potjie (pot) + kos (food)
Made in a cast-iron three-legged potjie pot over an open fire
The cast-iron three-legged pot was the central cooking vessel of the Voortrekkers
The potjie pot tradition: a layered stew cooked very slowly without stirring
The layering: meat on the bottom, then vegetables in layers (denser at bottom, softer on top)
The rule: do not stir -- the layers must remain intact
The condensation: the steam condenses on the lid and falls back in -- basting from above
Time: potjiekos takes 3-5 hours over low coals
The patience: the social event around the fire while waiting
South African wine poured in: Pinotage (South Africa unique red cultivar) or Shiraz
lunch.description: South African layered stew in a cast-iron three-legged pot (potjie) over open fire -- meat on the bottom, vegetables in layers above, cooked very slowly for 3-5 hours without stirring. The layers must remain intact; the steam recycles as condensation from the lid. The Voortrekker cast-iron pot tradition. South African wine (Pinotage or Shiraz) added during cooking. A social event: everyone waits around the fire.

lunch.name: Bobotie
ingredients: Dried fruit (apricots, raisins -- Cape Malay sweet-savory)
Bread soaked in milk (as a binder and softener)
instructions: Bobotie is South Africa national dish -- officially recognized
Cape Malay origin: the Indian-Malay community brought by Dutch colonizers to the Cape
The Cape Malay community: originally Indonesian and Malaysian slaves (1650s-1800s)
The sweet-savory combination: dried fruit in a meat dish -- Cape Malay signature
The bread soaked in milk is mixed into the meat -- adds moisture and softens
The curry powder: mild, not hot -- Cape Malay curry is aromatic, not fiery
The apricot and raisin: the sweet notes that define bobotie
The custard topping: eggs and milk poured over and baked -- sets as a golden layer
Bay leaves stuck upright into the custard -- the visual signature of bobotie
Served with geelrys (yellow saffron rice) and chutney
lunch.description: South Africa official national dish -- Cape Malay spiced and sweetened minced meat (beef or lamb with curry powder, dried apricots, raisins, and bread soaked in milk) topped with egg-milk custard and baked until the custard sets golden. Bay leaves stand upright as the visual signature. From the Cape Malay community (originally Indonesian-Malaysian): the sweet-savory combination is the Cape Malay signature. Served with geelrys (yellow saffron rice).

lunch.name: Cape Malay Curry
ingredients: Cape Malay masala blend: turmeric, coriander, cumin, fennel, cardamom, chilli
instructions: Cape Malay curry is distinct from Indian curry -- same origins, different evolution
The Cape Malay community: brought from Indonesia, Malaysia, and India to Cape Town (1650s+)
Isolated at the Cape, the community developed its own cuisine over 350 years
Cape Malay curry is aromatic and sweet-savory -- less fiery than Indian counterparts
The spice blend: turmeric, coriander, cumin, fennel, cardamom
Dried apricots: the sweet-savory accent specific to Cape Malay cooking
The Bo-Kaap: the Cape Malay neighborhood in Cape Town -- brightly painted houses
Bo-Kaap is the cultural center of the Cape Malay community
Cape Malay cooking also includes: koeksisters, samoosas, denningvleis (tamarind lamb)
lunch.description: Cape Town Cape Malay curry -- aromatic and sweet-savory (less fiery than Indian counterparts) with turmeric, coriander, cumin, fennel, and cardamom, and dried apricots as the sweet accent. The Cape Malay community (brought from Indonesia, Malaysia, and India from the 1650s) developed its own cuisine over 350 years in isolation at the Cape. The Bo-Kaap neighborhood in Cape Town is its cultural center.

dinner.name: Boboties Geelrys (Yellow Rice)
ingredients: Turmeric (the key -- for the yellow color and flavor)
instructions: Geelrys (yellow rice) is the traditional accompaniment to bobotie
Geelrys means yellow rice in Afrikaans: geel (yellow) + rys (rice)
The yellow color: turmeric added to the cooking water
The raisins cooked into the rice: the sweet-savory Cape Malay element
Cinnamon and bay leaf: aromatic notes in the rice
The sweetness of the raisins against the savory bobotie: the balance
A simple, beautifully colored rice that complements spiced dishes
dinner.description: South African Cape Malay yellow rice -- basmati rice cooked with turmeric (the yellow), cinnamon stick, bay leaf, and raisins (cooked in). The sweetness of the raisins and the aromatic turmeric are the Cape Malay signature. The traditional accompaniment to bobotie; also served with any Cape Malay curry.

dinner.name: Snoek Braai
ingredients: Snoek (South African barracouta -- a long, silvery firm fish)
Apricot jam or Mrs Balls chutney (the classic snoek braai marinade)
instructions: Snoek is the quintessential Cape Town fish -- caught in Cape waters
Snoek (Thyrsites atun): a long, silvery barracouta with firm, flavorful flesh
Braai snoek: the traditional Cape method -- cooked directly over fire
The marinade: apricot jam or Mrs Balls chutney (the famous South African chutney)
The sweet-tangy marinade caramelizes over the fire -- glazing the fish
The snoek flesh is firm and slightly smoky from the braai
Snoek season: winter and spring -- Cape Town fish market tradition
Smoked snoek pate: the other classic snoek preparation
Served with fresh white bread or vetkoek to soak up the juices
The Hout Bay harbor: the Cape Town fishing community center for snoek
dinner.description: Cape Town fish dish -- snoek (barracouta, caught in Cape waters) marinated in apricot jam or Mrs Balls chutney (the famous South African chutney), braai-grilled until the sweet-tangy glaze caramelizes. The firm, smoky flesh and the sweet glaze are the combination. Snoek season is winter and spring. Served with white bread or vetkoek. The Hout Bay harbor is the snoek fishing center.

dinner.name: Umngqusho (Samp and Beans)
ingredients: Samp (dried corn kernels -- cracked, not ground)
instructions: Umngqusho is the Xhosa and Zulu samp and beans -- one of South Africa oldest dishes
Samp: cracked dried corn kernels (not maize meal, not hominy -- a specific product)
Umngqusho was Nelson Mandela favorite food -- he requested it at state dinners
The Xhosa cultural connection: umngqusho was eaten at Xhosa celebrations and rites
Cowpeas or sugar beans: the legume that provides protein alongside the starch
The cooking: samp and beans must soak overnight, then cook for 2-3 hours
The long cooking: the samp and beans become tender and creamy
Seasoned simply -- the simplicity is the point
Umngqusho crosses cultural boundaries: also eaten in the Cape Malay tradition
dinner.description: South African Xhosa samp and beans -- cracked dried corn (samp) and cowpeas or sugar beans soaked overnight and slow-cooked for 2-3 hours until creamy and tender. Nelson Mandela favorite food; he requested it at state dinners. The Xhosa cultural staple for celebrations and rites. One of the oldest dishes in South Africa.

dinner.name: Biltong
ingredients: Beef (silverside or topside -- lean, trimmed of fat)
Coriander seed (crushed -- the defining biltong spice)
Brown sugar (small amount -- for flavor balance)
instructions: Biltong is the South African dried, cured meat -- not beef jerky (different process)
The distinction from jerky: biltong is cured in vinegar first, then air-dried (not smoked/cooked)
The coriander seed: the essential and defining biltong spice
Origin: the Voortrekkers who cured meat for the Great Trek as preserved food
The process: strips of meat are salted, spiced, vinegar-cured, then hung to air-dry
Air-drying: in a biltong box or in a cool, dry, windy environment
Drying time: 3-7 days depending on thickness and desired wetness
Wet biltong: soft, still has moisture -- preferred by many South Africans
Dry biltong: hard, fully dried -- keeps longer
Biltong is eaten as a snack at all South African events: sports, road trips, movies
dinner.description: South African air-dried cured meat -- beef strips vinegar-cured, then rubbed with salt, crushed coriander seed (the defining spice), and dried for 3-7 days. Not beef jerky: biltong is cured in vinegar then air-dried, not smoked or cooked. Voortrekker preserved food for the Great Trek. Wet biltong (still moist) and dry biltong (fully dried) are the two styles. Eaten at every South African occasion.

dinner.name: Braaibroodjie (Braai Toastie)
instructions: Braaibroodjie means braai bread in Afrikaans: braai + broodjie (small bread)
A cheese-tomato-onion toasted sandwich cooked directly over the braai coals
The classic: butter on the outside, cheese, tomato, onion, and chutney inside
Mrs Balls chutney: the iconic South African condiment -- sweet peach-based chutney
The braaibroodjie is placed directly on the grid over the dying coals
Cooked until golden and pressed -- the cheese melts, the bread chars slightly
The slight char from the braai: essential to the flavor
The timing: braaibroodjie goes on at the end of the braai, on the dying coals
Eaten while the fire dies and people wind down -- the social epilogue of the braai
dinner.description: South African braai toasted sandwich -- thick white bread buttered on the outside, filled with cheddar or gouda, sliced tomato, onion, and Mrs Balls chutney (the iconic sweet peach chutney), grilled directly on the braai grid over dying coals until golden and slightly charred. Goes on at the end of the braai; the social epilogue while the fire dies.

snacks.name: Droewors (Dried Sausage)
instructions: Droewors means dried sausage in Afrikaans: droog (dry) + wors (sausage)
Made from the same spiced beef mixture as boerewors, but formed into thinner sausages
The thinner diameter allows faster and more even drying
Air-dried like biltong -- hung to dry for 3-5 days
The coriander seed: the essential droewors spice, same as boerewors
The result: a dry, snappy sausage with intense concentrated flavor
Eaten as a snack alongside biltong -- the two always appear together
South African sports events: biltong and droewors are the stadium snacks
The texture difference from biltong: sausage-shaped, casings, snappier
snacks.description: South African dried spiced sausage -- boerewors mixture (beef with coriander seed, cloves, nutmeg) formed into thinner sausages and air-dried for 3-5 days until dry and snappy. The coriander seed is the defining flavor. Always paired with biltong at South African sports events and social gatherings. The casing gives a snap that biltong does not have.

snacks.name: Koeksisters (Cape Malay)
ingredients: Flour, yeast, milk, egg, butter (for the dough)
Cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, anise (Cape Malay spices)
instructions: Cape Malay koeksisters are different from Afrikaner koeksisters -- completely different item
Afrikaner koeksisters: braided deep-fried dough soaked in cold sugar syrup (crispy)
Cape Malay koeksisters: round, spiced dough balls, dipped in syrup, rolled in coconut (soft)
Same name, different dish -- a source of cheerful confusion
The Cape Malay spices: cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, anise -- aromatic and warm
Soft and pillowy inside from the yeast dough
The coconut coating: desiccated coconut pressed onto the syrup-soaked surface
Made on Saturday mornings in Bo-Kaap (the Cape Malay neighborhood)
Sold door-to-door in Bo-Kaap every Saturday -- the weekend tradition
snacks.description: Cape Malay spiced doughnut -- round yeast-dough balls spiced with cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, and anise, deep-fried until golden, dipped in sugar syrup, rolled in desiccated coconut. Completely different from Afrikaner koeksisters (braided, cold-syrup-soaked). Made on Saturday mornings in Bo-Kaap (Cape Town Cape Malay neighborhood) and sold door-to-door -- the weekend tradition.

snacks.name: Milk Tart (Melktert)
ingredients: Milk, eggs, sugar, flour or cornstarch
instructions: Melktert (milk tart) is the Afrikaner dessert tart -- one of South Africa most beloved
Melktert means milk tart in Afrikaans: melk (milk) + tert (tart)
Essentially a custard tart with South African proportion: more milk, lighter set
The filling is a milk-egg-sugar custard -- lighter than French crème patissiere
The cinnamon dusting on top: the essential finishing touch of melktert
Two versions: baked set (the custard is baked in the pastry) and fridge set
Fridge set melktert: the custard is cooked, then poured cold into the pastry case
Sold at every South African church bazaar and school bake sale
The church bazaar: a South African tradition -- community fundraising with baked goods
snacks.description: Afrikaner milk custard tart -- a shortcrust pastry shell filled with a light, milky custard (more milk than egg: lighter than crème patissiere), dusted generously with cinnamon. The cinnamon is essential. Two versions: baked set and fridge set (cold custard poured cold). At every South African church bazaar and school bake sale. One of the most beloved South African desserts.

snacks.name: Chakalaka
instructions: Chakalaka is the South African township relish -- spiced tomato and bean
Origin: Soweto and South African townships -- created from affordable, accessible ingredients
The township grocery store ingredients: canned beans, tomatoes, carrots, onion
Chakalaka is hot, spicy, and very flavorful -- the counterpoint to the simplicity of pap
Curry powder and chilli: the heat and warmth
Butter beans or baked beans: the protein and substance
Chakalaka accompanies: pap, braai meat, bread, and almost anything else
Every South African family has a chakalaka recipe -- no two are the same
snacks.description: South African township spiced relish -- tomatoes, onions, butter beans, grated carrots, and peppers with curry powder and chilli. Origin: Soweto townships, made from affordable available ingredients. Accompanies pap, braai meat, and bread. No two family recipes are the same.

imageCredit.author: philipp from cape town, south africa

desserts.name: Malva Pudding
ingredients: Cream sauce (cream, butter, sugar -- poured hot over the hot pudding)
instructions: Malva pudding is the Cape Dutch baked sponge pudding -- deeply loved
The name origin: uncertain -- malva is the marshmallow plant, but the connection is unclear
The apricot jam: mixed into the batter -- gives the characteristic slight sweetness
Bicarbonate of soda + vinegar: the chemical leavening that gives lift
The vinegar: adds a subtle tang and also reacts with the bicarb
The cream sauce: the most important element -- poured over the hot pudding
The cream sauce (made with cream, butter, and sugar) is poured over while both are hot
The sauce is absorbed into the pudding -- the pudding becomes saturated and rich
Malva pudding is served warm -- essentially at every South African restaurant
Also made at home: the comfort dessert after Sunday braai
desserts.description: South African Cape Dutch baked sponge pudding -- batter with apricot jam (the signature sweetness), bicarbonate of soda, and vinegar, baked until golden, then drenched with hot cream sauce (cream, butter, sugar) that is absorbed into the pudding while both are hot. Served warm. At every South African restaurant. The comfort dessert after Sunday braai. The cream sauce absorption is the technique.

desserts.name: Melktert (Milk Tart)
ingredients: Full cream milk, eggs, sugar, cornstarch or flour
instructions: Melktert is South Africa most beloved home-baking staple
Melk = milk, tert = tart in Afrikaans
The defining characteristic: more milk than egg -- a lighter, less rich custard than French tarts
The cinnamon dusting is non-negotiable -- melktert without cinnamon is just a custard tart
Two methods: baked (custard baked in pastry) and fridge-set (cooked custard poured cold)
The fridge-set version is more common at home -- no risk of soggy bottom
Sold at every Cape Malay spice market, church bazaar, and school fundraiser
The flavor is gentle, milky, warm with cinnamon -- comfort in dessert form
desserts.description: South African milk custard tart -- light custard (more milk than egg: the signature lightness) in a shortcrust shell, dusted with cinnamon (non-negotiable). Baked or fridge-set (cooked custard poured cold into pastry). At every church bazaar and school bake sale. The defining dessert of Afrikaner home-baking.

desserts.name: Hertzoggies (Apricot Jam Tarts)
ingredients: Sugar, egg whites (for the coconut meringue topping)
instructions: Hertzoggies are South African jam tarts with a coconut meringue topping
Named after Barry Hertzog, South African Prime Minister (1924-1939)
The naming: the origin is disputed, but the political naming is part of South African culinary history
The base: a shortcrust pastry case
The filling: apricot jam (the South African jam of choice)
The topping: a coconut meringue -- whipped egg whites with desiccated coconut
The coconut meringue is spooned onto the jam and baked until set and golden
The combination: the tartness of the apricot jam against the sweet coconut meringue
Found at: every South African koek (bake) tradition, alongside melktert and koeksisters
desserts.description: South African apricot jam tarts with coconut meringue -- shortcrust pastry base, filled with apricot jam, topped with coconut meringue (egg whites and desiccated coconut), baked until set and golden. Named after Barry Hertzog, Prime Minister (1924-1939). The tartness of the apricot jam against the sweet coconut meringue. At every South African bake sale alongside melktert and koeksisters.

drinks.name: Rooibos Tea
ingredients: Rooibos (red bush -- Aspalathus linearis, indigenous to the Cederberg mountains of the Western Cape)
instructions: Rooibos (red bush) is the South African herbal tea -- indigenous to South Africa alone
Aspalathus linearis: only grows in the Cederberg Mountains of the Western Cape
The Khoisan people: the indigenous San and Khoikhoi used rooibos long before colonization
The color: brews a rich red -- the oxidation of the rooibos leaves
No caffeine: unlike black tea -- rooibos is caffeine-free naturally
No tannins: unlike black tea -- less bitter, can steep indefinitely
Flavor: slightly sweet, nutty, herbal -- distinct from any other tea
Green rooibos: unoxidized, lighter color and flavor
South Africa exports rooibos worldwide -- but it can only be grown in the Cederberg
Rooibos latte, rooibos iced tea: the modern versions
drinks.description: South African indigenous herbal tea -- rooibos (red bush, Aspalathus linearis) grows only in the Cederberg Mountains of the Western Cape. The Khoisan people used it before colonization. Caffeine-free, no tannins, brews a rich red. The flavor is slightly sweet, nutty, and herbal. South Africa exports rooibos worldwide but it can only be grown in the Cederberg.

drinks.name: Amarula Cream Liqueur
ingredients: Amarula liqueur (made from the fruit of the marula tree -- Sclerocarya birrea)
instructions: Amarula is the South African cream liqueur made from the marula fruit
The marula tree: Sclerocarya birrea -- indigenous to southern Africa
The marula fruit: a yellow-green fruit that falls from the tree when ripe
The elephants and marula: the famous story that elephants get drunk on fermented marulas
The elephant story is a myth -- elephants would need to eat enormous quantities
But the marula-elephant connection is part of South African wildlife folklore
The flavor: caramel, butterscotch, tropical fruit -- rich and sweet
Made by Distell in South Africa since 1989
The Amarula elephant: the logo -- the elephant on the label
Drunk on ice, in coffee, in cream liqueur cocktails
drinks.description: South African marula cream liqueur -- made from the fruit of the marula tree (indigenous to southern Africa), fermented and distilled, then blended with cream. Rich caramel-butterscotch-tropical flavor. The marula-elephant story (that elephants get drunk on fermented fruit) is South African wildlife folklore, though largely a myth. Made since 1989; the elephant is the logo.

drinks.name: Pinotage Wine
ingredients: Pinotage (South Africa unique red grape varietal -- a cross of Pinot Noir and Cinsault)
instructions: Pinotage is the South African grape -- a variety that exists nowhere else in the world
Created by Dr Abraham Perold at Stellenbosch University in 1925
A crossing of Pinot Noir and Cinsault (then called Hermitage in South Africa)
Pinotage = Pinot + Hermitage: the name preserves the parent varieties
The flavor: earthy, smoky, dark fruit (plum, blackberry), with a distinctive savory note
The controversy: some Pinotage can have a paint-like note (ethyl acetate) -- the quality indicator
Well-made Pinotage: complex, full-bodied, distinctly South African
The wine estates: Stellenbosch, Paarl, Franschhoek -- the Cape Winelands
Cape Winelands: European viticulture transplanted to the Cape (1655 by Jan van Riebeeck)
drinks.description: South Africa unique red grape variety -- created by Dr Abraham Perold at Stellenbosch University in 1925 by crossing Pinot Noir and Cinsault (called Hermitage: hence Pinotage). Exists nowhere else. Earthy, smoky, dark fruit flavors; well-made bottles are complex and full-bodied. The Cape Winelands (Stellenbosch, Paarl, Franschhoek) were established 1655 by Jan van Riebeeck.
